alternatives.name: LG Energy Solution (Holland and Lansing, Michigan)

parts.risk_note: Cells are the biggest cost and most China-concentrated part, prices turned up in 2026, and tax credit eligibility now depends on how much of the cell content traces to China.

our_read.label: Price and rules

parts.name: Inverter and power electronics (IGBT, Si MOSFET, SiC MOSFET)
parts.what_it_does: Converts battery DC to home AC and back, and does the grid-forming switching. Base describes its Austin plant as a power electronics hub.

lead_time.quote: while power device lead times have generally stretched beyond 30 weeks, with some reaching 52 weeks.

price_trend.value: Infineon raised power device prices twice in 2026, July round 10-20%; ST third hike of 2026 from Aug 23
price_trend.quote: lifting AI server power and automotive power device prices by 10%-20%.

concentration.value: SiC substrates 2024: Wolfspeed 33.7%, China's TanKeBlue 17.3% and SICC 17.1%
concentration.quote: Wolfspeed first with a 33.7% market share
concentration.note: 2024 data; Wolfspeed went through Chapter 11 in mid-2025. No IGBT/MOSFET share data collected (not found).

alternatives.name: Infineon, onsemi, STMicroelectronics, Wolfspeed
alternatives.note: Non-China IGBT/MOSFET/SiC sources, all raising prices in 2026.

alternatives.name: Chinese IGBT makers (MacMic, JieJie)
alternatives.note: Also raising 10-20%, and carry 50% Section 301 duty.

parts.risk_note: Power semiconductors are on 30 to 52 week lead times with three rounds of 2026 price hikes, so inverter builds need parts ordered most of a year ahead.

our_read.label: Long wait
our_read.why: Order most of a year ahead. Power chips are the longest lead item inside the box.

parts.name: Battery management system and control electronics (MCU, DRAM, NAND/eMMC)
parts.what_it_does: Measures cell voltages and temperatures, balances cells, runs the controller and stores firmware and logs. Uses small, mostly legacy memory parts (DDR4, LPDDR4, eMMC) plus microcontrollers.

lead_time.value: 32-40+ weeks for standard DDR4 and DDR5 modules in some cases, under allocation
lead_time.quote: lead times on standard DDR4 and DDR5 modules have already stretched to 32-40+ weeks in some cases
lead_time.source_quality: vendor blog behind a bot check; quote not verified by us

price_trend.quote: Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 45-50% QoQ

more.quote: with conventional DRAM prices expected to surge 90-95% QoQ

We believe that the aggregate industry supply will remain substantially short of the demand for the foreseeable future.

price_trend.conflict: One secondary report (StockHub, 2026-10-20) says TrendForce later put 4Q26 DRAM near +20%; not verified on TrendForce.

concentration.value: Allocation goes to AI and server first; industrial and consumer DDR4 users rank last
concentration.quote: Memory suppliers continue to prioritize capacity allocation toward higher-margin AI and server products

more.quote: ranks behind PC and server applications in suppliers' allocation priorities.

concentration.share_note: DRAM is made mainly by Samsung, SK hynix and Micron; no dated share quote collected (not found in this pass).

policy.name: Section 232 semiconductors, phase 1 (Proclamation 11002)
policy.status: in effect since 2026-01-15, but only for advanced AI-class chips; broader phase 2 possible
policy.value: 25% on chips above performance thresholds; not BMS-class parts
policy.quote: The tariff applies only to semiconductors meeting specific technical performance thresholds, not to all semiconductor imports.

alternatives.name: Winbond, Nanya and other Taiwanese DDR4 makers
alternatives.note: Still producing DDR4 as Micron, Samsung and SK hynix exit; TrendForce says their expansion cannot fully offset the cut.

alternatives.name: Design out discrete DRAM
alternatives.note: MCUs with on-chip SRAM and flash avoid buying commodity DRAM at all.

parts.risk_note: The memory in a battery controller is cheap in dollars but sits at the back of the allocation line behind AI servers, so the risk is a missing part, not a big cost hit.

our_read.label: Allocation
our_read.why: Small and cheap, and many battery controllers use microcontrollers with memory built in. Where a design does need separate memory chips, they are last in line behind AI servers.

parts.name: Cellular modem / connectivity module
parts.what_it_does: Lets the fleet operator dispatch the battery and push firmware. Base's business model (virtual power plant) depends on it.

concentration.value: Top five module makers (Quectel, Fibocom, Telit Cinterion, MeiG, China Mobile IoT) held 73% of revenue in 2025; China-based suppliers lead on volume

all recorded steady increases in Q2, however.

about: One home battery, part by part: how long each part takes to get, where prices are heading, where it comes from, and which 2026 US rules touch it. Every number links to a dated public source. "Our read" is this site's judgment, not a source. Independent, not affiliated with Base Power.
